questions.q: What is the basic structural composition of a virus particle (virion)?
a: A central core of genetic material (DNA or RNA) surrounded by a protein coat (capsid)
A complete eukaryotic cell with a nucleus and cytoplasm
A bacterial cell wall enclosing chloroplasts
A droplet of lipids with no genetic material

questions.q: Why are viruses not classified as living organisms by most biologists?
a: They are too large to see with a microscope
They lack cellular structure, do not respire, cannot feed, and cannot reproduce independently outside a living host cell
They do not contain any genetic material
They are exclusively beneficial to ecosystems

questions.q: How do viruses reproduce (replicate)?
a: By binary fission like bacteria
By producing sexual gametes and spores
By invading a living host cell and hijacking the host's cellular machinery to make copies of viral components
By absorbing nutrients from soil water

questions.q: What term is used to describe a virus that specifically infects and destroys bacterial cells?
a: Retrovirus
Pathogenic yeast
Saprophytic bacterium
Bacteriophage

questions.q: What is the protective protein shell that encloses the viral genetic material called?
a: Capsid
Cell wall
Plasma membrane
Nucleus

questions.q: Which of the following diseases in humans is caused by a viral infection?
a: Tuberculosis
Influenza (flu)
Strep throat
Cholera

questions.q: What distinguishes the genetic material of viruses from that of living cellular organisms?
a: Viruses always contain both double-stranded DNA and RNA simultaneously
Viral genetic material is stored inside a true membrane-bound nucleus
Viral genetic material can be DNA or RNA, which may be single-stranded or double-stranded depending on the virus type
Viruses contain no nucleic acids

questions.q: Why are antibiotics ineffective against viral infections such as the common cold or influenza?
a: Because antibiotics are too expensive
Because viruses are too big for antibiotics to touch
Because antibiotics target bacterial cell walls, ribosomes, or bacterial metabolic pathways, which viruses do not possess
Because viruses destroy antibiotics instantly

questions.q: What is an outer envelope found on certain viruses (like HIV or Influenza) typically composed of?
a: A phospholipid membrane stolen from the host cell's membrane, embedded with viral proteins
A rigid layer of cellulose
Thick layers of peptidoglycan
Pure crystalline chitin

questions.q: How do antiviral drugs work to combat viral diseases?
a: By destroying the human immune system
By interfering with viral replication mechanisms, such as blocking viral enzymes or preventing viral entry into host cells
By dissolving the human cell wall
By acting as a direct physical disinfectant on skin

questions.q: What is the typical size range of virus particles compared to bacteria?
a: Viruses are much larger than bacteria
Viruses are roughly the same size as plant cells
Viruses are extremely microscopic, typically much smaller than bacteria (ranging from 20 to 400 nanometers)
Viruses can be seen easily with the naked eye

questions.q: Which of the following plant diseases is caused by a virus?
a: Potato blight (caused by a fungus-like organism)
Powdery mildew
Black stem rust of wheat
Tobacco mosaic disease (Tobacco Mosaic Virus)

questions.q: What happens immediately after a virus attaches to a host cell and injects or enters its genetic material?
a: The host cell's machinery is hijacked to transcribe and translate viral genes, producing new viral proteins and nucleic acids
The virus immediately undergoes photosynthesis
The host cell divides rapidly into healthy twins
The virus turns into a bacterium

questions.q: What is the term for the stage where newly assembled virus particles cause the host cell to burst open (lysis), releasing them to infect other cells?
a: Lysogenic dormancy
Lytic cycle (cell lysis)
Binary fission
Conjugation

questions.q: How does vaccination protect humans against viral infections?
a: By curing an active viral infection instantly
By killing all bacteria in the stomach
By introducing weakened or inactivated viral antigens (or genetic instructions) to stimulate primary immune response and memory cell production
By changing human DNA permanently

questions.q: Which of the following describes human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)?
a: A bacterium that infects red blood cells
A fungus that attacks skin tissue
A harmless spore found in soil
A retrovirus that infects white blood cells (T-helper cells) and can lead to AIDS

questions.q: Why do viruses mutate rapidly, making the creation of long-lasting vaccines for viruses like influenza challenging?
a: Their replication enzymes (especially in RNA viruses) often lack proofreading mechanisms, leading to high error rates during genetic copying
They eat mutagenic chemicals in the blood
They grow larger every year
They perform sexual reproduction constantly

questions.q: What is the primary reason viral infections cannot be cultured on nutrient agar plates in the same way bacteria are grown?
a: Agar plates are too cold
Viruses require living host cells to multiply and cannot grow on non-living nutrient broth or agar
Bacteria eat the viruses instantly
Viruses require sunlight to grow on agar

questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic feature shared by all viruses?
a: Presence of cytoplasm and ribosomes
Ability to carry out independent respiration
Parasitic nature requiring a living host cell for replication
Ability to move using flagella

questions.q: How are viruses generally transmitted between human hosts?
a: Through photosynthesis and root absorption
By magnetic radiation
Through gravitational pull
Via droplets from coughs/sneezes, bodily fluids, contaminated water/food, or insect vectors

questions.q: What is a 'provirus' or 'prophage' in the lysogenic cycle of viral replication?
a: Viral DNA that has integrated into the host cell's chromosome and replicates quietly along with host cell division
A fully formed virus ready to burst the cell
A dead virus particle
A bacterial defense enzyme

questions.q: Which viral disease historically caused severe global epidemics marked by skin pustules before being successfully eradicated worldwide through vaccination programs?
a: Rabies
Smallpox
Common cold
Ebola

questions.q: What is the role of surface glycoproteins (spikes) on the outer surface of many viruses?
a: To store energy for the virus
To digest food particles outside the host
To bind specifically to receptor molecules on the surface of target host cells, facilitating entry
To perform photosynthesis

questions.q: Which of the following statements accurately contrasts bacteria and viruses?
a: Both are living cellular organisms that reproduce by mitosis
Bacteria are non-living, whereas viruses are living cells
Viruses possess cell walls made of peptidoglycan, whereas bacteria have capsids
Bacteria are living single-celled organisms with cellular machinery and metabolism, whereas viruses are non-cellular infectious agents requiring a host

questions.q: Why is the common cold so difficult to cure with a single vaccine or drug?
a: Because hundreds of different types of rhinoviruses and other viruses cause cold symptoms, and they mutate easily
Because colds are caused by bacteria
Because cold viruses have thick cell walls
Because cold viruses live forever in soil

questions.q: What does the term 'pathogen' mean, and why do viruses fit this description?
a: A pathogen is a nutrient molecule; viruses provide energy to cells
A pathogen is any disease-causing microorganism or agent, and viruses cause infectious diseases in plants and animals
A pathogen is a beneficial white blood cell
A pathogen is a plant hormone

questions.q: In scientific research, how are viruses safely studied or used in biotechnology?
a: By growing them in open laboratory air
By feeding them sugar water in glass beakers
By culturing them inside living tissue cultures, embryonated eggs, or using them as vectors in genetic engineering
By boiling them in test tubes

questions.q: Which viral infection affects the nervous system and can cause paralysis if unvaccinated?
a: Polio (Poliomyelitis)
Malaria
Athlete's foot
Scurvy

questions.q: What structural feature do some advanced viruses (like bacteriophages) possess that aids in injecting their DNA into a host cell?
a: A protein tail sheath and tail fibers
A long muscular flagellum
Cellulose cilia
A chitinous exoskeleton

questions.q: Why do epidemiological scientists track viral mutations closely during global outbreaks?
a: To determine the color of the virus
To monitor changes in transmissibility, virulence, and vaccine effectiveness
To calculate the weight of infected hosts
To name new virus strains alphabetically

questions.q: What happens to a host cell after the lytic cycle of a virulent virus is completed?
a: The host cell becomes stronger and immune
The host cell lives indefinitely
The host cell is destroyed (lysed) as new viruses break out
The host cell turns into a plant cell

questions.q: Which of the following viral infections is primarily transmitted through the bite of an infected animal (such as a dog or bat) and affects the central nervous system?
a: Measles
Chickenpox
Influenza
Rabies

questions.q: What is the primary function of viral enzymes (such as reverse transcriptase in retroviruses) packaged inside the capsid?
a: To assist in specific steps of viral replication and transcription inside the host cell
To digest food for the virus
To produce oxygen for the virus
To build bacterial cell walls

questions.q: How can the spread of viral waterborne or foodborne diseases (like Hepatitis A or Norovirus) be effectively prevented in communities?
a: By taking massive doses of penicillin
By ensuring proper sanitation, sewage treatment, boiling drinking water, and practicing good hand hygiene
By exposing water supplies to bright sunlight
By eliminating all bacteria from soil

questions.q: Why are viruses considered obligate intracellular parasites?
a: They can live freely in seawater without any host
They only parasitize other viruses
They are strictly dependent on living inside a host cell to reproduce and carry out any biological activity
They require sunlight to survive

questions.q: Which of the following viral infections causes characteristic rashes and blisters on the skin and is caused by the varicella-zoster virus?
a: Rabies
Hiv
Ebola
Chickenpox

questions.q: What occurs during the assembly stage of viral replication?
a: Newly synthesized viral genetic material and protein capsids are put together to form mature virus particles (virions)
The host cell divides by mitosis
The virus absorbs water and grows larger
Viral proteins are broken down into amino acids

questions.q: Why do public health organizations recommend annual flu vaccinations?
a: Because influenza vaccines expire after 24 hours
Because influenza viruses undergo antigenic drift (mutation), requiring updated vaccines each year to match circulating strains
Because flu shots cure bacterial pneumonia
Because flu viruses turn into bacteria every winter

questions.q: Which characteristic of life is completely absent in free-standing virus particles outside a host?
a: Having a protein coat
Containing genetic material
Metabolism, respiration, and independent reproduction
Having a microscopic size
